title: Rescue breaths during adult CPR
intro: This guide concerns an adult who is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Call 112 immediately for an unresponsive person, use speakerphone and follow the dispatcher. Do not delay resuscitation to read an article; practical training builds confidence.

sections.heading: Recognize an emergency and call
paragraphs: Check the scene is safe, speak to the person and assess responsiveness. While emergency help is called, check breathing. Occasional gasps are not normal breathing. If unresponsive with abnormal breathing, start CPR and ask someone to bring an AED.

sections.heading: Start adult chest compressions
paragraphs: For adult chest compressions, put the heel of a hand in the center of the chest with the other hand above it. Keep arms straight, press 5–6 cm deep at 100–120 compressions per minute, and allow full recoil with minimal interruptions.

sections.heading: Give breaths if trained and able
paragraphs: If trained and able, alternate 30 compressions with 2 breaths. Open the airway with head tilt and chin lift, pinch the nose, seal your mouth over theirs and blow gently for about 1 second, just enough for the chest to rise. Let it fall before the next breath.

sections.heading: Minimize interruptions
paragraphs: Keep the interruption for breaths below 10 seconds. If breaths fail, do not keep making prolonged attempts: return to compressions and follow dispatcher advice. If unable or unwilling to give breaths, continue chest compressions; doing something promptly is better than waiting.

sections.heading: Use an AED and continue help
paragraphs: Apply an AED as soon as available and follow its prompts; nobody should touch the person during analysis or shock. Continue until professionals take over, normal breathing returns, the scene becomes unsafe or you cannot continue. Children, infants and drowning need tailored instructions, especially about breaths.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira calls emergency help on speakerphone while a helper brings an AED. She follows the dispatcher instead of spending time searching for a pulse.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben cannot provide rescue breaths. He continues compressions while following instructions, rather than stopping all help because mouth-to-mouth is not possible.
